review_comments: We should use a type guard here also.
And probably clean up this whole file to use guards.
The non-null assertion here is necessary, because `strictNullChecks` flags uncalled functions inside `if` statements as of a few TS versions ago.
But it is not necessary if you put this inside a type-guard.

Isn't this a breaking change? `Function` doesn't seem to be assignable to this new type: https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?#code/DYUwLgBAZgXBBiBXAdgYzASwPbIgXmhXW2QAooss5lEBbAIxACcBKCAbwifESdwqwBqQRAC+AbgBQoSFFgRSYABYYAznABuWDABMANBAB0xgIZMA5uognkATwDaAXTZ4AfNbv5CaTDnKVqOkZWDi4ePmhKYTEpSTkvKHEgA

You're right that it technically could break, but I think that it's unlikely. The signature change wasn't strictly necessary, but we agreed to do it because it prevents users from writing code that might break after compilation. We could roll back the signature change and leave it for the next major version, if we find that it's too break-ey.

Do we need to concern ourselves with the binding of `this` in such a method declaration?
For example, would such a methed ever be analysed by the partial evaluator? In which case the use of `this` inside the method would be affected if this function expression was treated as unbound.
Would it work to store the method declaration directly rather than synthesizing a new function expression node, given that the translator does have logic to handle `visitInvokeMethodExpr()`?

I don't think we have to concern ourselves with `this` since it's inside an object literal where it doesn't make sense. Also I don't think that we can store the method declaration directly, because:
1. Storing the method would produce different code, compared to a `FunctionExpression` (e.g. `useFactory() {}` vs `function useFactory() {}`).
2. The typings expect an `Expression`. It probably won't be too difficult to fix, but we'd have to update a lot of places.

> I don't think we have to concern ourselves with this since it's inside an object literal where it doesn't make sense.

I am not sure I agree with this. It is certainly possible to refer to other fields in the object literal via `this` in such a method. Try running this [TS playground](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?#code/MYewdgzgLgBAHjAvDA3gKBjAhgLhgRgAYAaDGAMxBAAoBKVMzUSEAGwFMA6VkAc2qgALAJYROWWgG4yAXzRy0cTpRq0gA).

I agree that we can't store the method declaration directly. I think we would need to store a function that is bound to the appropriate `this`. I am not sure the best approach but two alternatives would be:

```
() => { obj.useFactory(); }
// where we would have to synthesize and pass through the parameters
```

or

```
useFactory.bind(obj)()
```

How would we get a reference to `obj` though? We'd have to move the object into a variable that would be passed into `bind` and the `factory` property. I think that it complicates the compiler unnecessarily, considering that the only other property that is allowed on the object literal is `providedIn`.

This function `reflectObjectLiteral()` is used for pretty much all of the decorators. But from a quick look through it seems like most if not all of the decorators do not allow functions as properties of the decorator metadata (except for this exception). Perhaps that is why this has not come up before?

So, OK at the moment I guess this would be adding unnecessary complexity to the compiler. But I am worried that it would be confusing for the developer if we do not follow the semantics of the code - perhaps in the future. I wonder if we could do an assertion that there are no references to `this` in the body of the function when reflecting on such a method before outputting it as a free standing function?
I think that typing the `InjectableOptions` interface is a great idea. Catches the problem really early on in the developer experience.
+1 for constraining the type of `useFactory` to infer `this: never` in these cases.
Changed the type to `(this: never, ...args: any[]) => any`.

This is the first time we create TS nodes in a `ReflectionHost`. Generally the host is "readonly" and I am worried this might have repercussions later on.  But perhaps this is OK...
It is a shame that we cannot just add the `ts.MethodDeclaration` to the map directly and then let the translator worry about it later.
I agree, the `ReflectionHost` should not be doing this kind of operation. It should return "ground truth" data about the source, and the consumer should perform this operation.
@alxhub do you have any ideas on how we can remove it though? The trouble is that in the translator the node is hidden in a `WrappedNodeExpr`...

@petebacondarwin @alxhub I've been looking at removing the `createFunctionExpression` call from here, but it'll involve updating the types all across the compiler and potentially losing some type safety. The problem is that this function (`reflectObjectLiteral`) returns a `Map<string, Expression>`, but a `MethodDeclaration` doesn't fit into the `Expression` interface so we can't assign it. The type would have to updated to `Map<string, Node>` which is less strict and it'll involve changing a lot of code since `reflectObjectLiteral` is used all over the compiler.

I see a couple of alternatives:
1. The return value can be changed to `Map<string, Expression|MethodDeclaration>`, but we'll have to add casts to all the places where we currently expect an `Expression` (about 25 places).
2. We can have a function similar to `reflectObjectLiteral` that returns `Map<string, Expression|MethodDeclaration>` and is only used in the relevant places, but then we'd have two functions that basically do the same thing.

What do you think? I wanted to double check before making all these extra changes.

I really don't like doing this parenthesis wrapping here. In general this is done in the translator. E.g. in [`visitWriteVarExpr`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3ba97ab3917b682b6d08b9e71599051e77e2d3ac/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/translator/src/translator.ts#L131-L132). 

But I can see that at the point when we are dealing with this call, in the translator, we don't know what this node is - it is a `WrappedNodeExpr`, which is opaque to the translator.

So I don't know if there is a better solution.

If we go with this then there should be an appropriate test added in [typescript_ast_factory_spec.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3082f7378b9fd620e11908e4cb0924681f9dea3b/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/translator/test/typescript_ast_factory_spec.ts#L69-L81).
This logic used to be in the translator, but I had to move it out after the changes that made it generic and I couldn't find a way to infer the node type.
